name: DEADLINE Next
pitch: Open-ended coding tasks with no top score. Every answer must be correct; better answers score higher.

scoring.headline: 100 x the mean over families of the mean over their tasks

integrity.title: Hidden tests come later
integrity.body: Hidden instances are made from a fresh seed only after the model has finished.

integrity.title: Locked sandbox
integrity.body: Answers run in Docker with no network, a read-only disk, one CPU and 512 MB.

integrity.title: Checked twice
integrity.body: Batch families have two independent checkers that must agree on every audit answer.

integrity.title: Transcripts reviewed
integrity.body: Every tool call is logged, and calls that touch paths outside the room are flagged.

integrity.title: No judge model
integrity.body: Every score is computed by code. No language model grades anything.

rules: A simple valid answer always exists, so no task is impossible.
A broken answer scores below the lazy answer, so careless work costs points.
Rooms hold the exact checker and scorer, so a model can measure itself.
Token budget and a 60-minute stop per task; wall time is recorded, never scored.

families.name: Shape to recipe
families.asks: Rebuild a 3D voxel shape as the shortest exact recipe of solids.
tests: testing against its own practice shapes

families.name: Strategy arena
families.asks: Write a bot for a two-player grid war game and beat five public bots.
families.cost: turns to destroy the enemy base, else a damage penalty
families.ref: the best ladder bot in that seat

families.name: Truck loading
families.asks: Load every box into a truck as low as possible, respecting gravity and delivery order.
families.floor: towers in lanes, later stops at the back
families.ref: an extreme-point packer, best of 44 orders

families.name: Dispatch
families.asks: Route vans to drop-offs and pickup pairs inside time windows and shifts.
families.cost: fee per van plus driven distance
families.floor: jobs by deadline, each added to the newest van if it fits

tiers.title: Dispatch (small)
tiers.size: 16 to 20 drops and 4 to 6 pickup pairs

tiers.title: Dispatch (medium)
tiers.size: 32 to 40 drops and 8 to 12 pickup pairs

tiers.title: Dispatch (large)
tiers.size: 55 to 65 drops and 15 to 20 pickup pairs

families.name: Factory scheduling
families.asks: Schedule every job step on factory machines with setups and maintenance.
families.cost: weighted finish times plus 5x weighted lateness
families.floor: each step appended on its earliest-finishing machine
families.ref: a list scheduler over many priority rules

families.name: Fast code
families.asks: Rewrite a correct but slow program so it gives the same output faster.

tiers.title: Fast code: Prefix matches under edits (medium)
Fast code: Shortest paths under edits (large)

families.name: Compression
families.asks: Write a compressor and decompressor for one kind of structured text.
families.cost: bytes of the blob plus a share of the program size
families.ref: the best of lzma, bz2 and zlib

tiers.title: Compression: game replay JSON lines (large)
tiers.size: game replay JSON lines, about 110-180 KB

families.name: Page layout
families.asks: Lay out articles, images and ads on a fixed-width page that Chrome measures.
families.ref: the best of 28 measured column and float layouts

release_gates: The lazy answer scores 0 and the reference scores 1 on fresh instances, within 0.02.
One model run three times has a spread below 5 headline points.
The top two models differ by more than their spread.
No task kind gives every model scores within 5 points of each other.
Every checker agrees with an independent checker on all public and audit instances.
